text: SUPERVISOR: RAMPCHAIN-0608 — USER, build placement adjacency gap, verbatim: "as it stands, you cant do this: ramp -> ramp / ramp -> floor. you can do tho wall -> ramp -> floor. but you should be able to do the first two also. and note its not like im saying 2 ramps next to each other. im saying running up the ramp, and then placing another ramp at the top of it to keep going up. or a floor." DIAGNOSIS: the placement/snap grammar does not expose a ramp's TOP (high) edge as an attach anchor. You can attach a ramp to a wall below it (wall->ramp->floor works), but from the top of a ramp you cannot continue with another ramp (keep ascending) or a floor (land flat at the new height). Add the ramp's top edge as a valid snap SOURCE for both ramp (continue up at the elevated height) and floor (cap it flat). This is NOT side-by-side ramps — it is vertical chaining off the high end: the next piece starts at the ramp top's elevation. Print the ramp's registered snap anchors vs what wall/floor expose, find why the top edge is absent, add it. Frame-time gate applies if collision registration changes. Queue this with the building-bug cluster you are on (it is the same placement/build domain) — do not drop the cluster diagnosis.
